name: @brilliant-hq/mcp

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Get the IDs and blueprint of currently selected elements on a specific canvas. Returns selected element IDs and their blueprint representation including descendants. A selection past 1,000 elements (descendants included) is summarized: counts by type (`countsByType`), union bounds (`worldBounds`), the first 100 ids and a `note`, beside the true `count`. Use `read` with a `scope` of ids or #refs for full subtrees. (External MCP clients: call `init` first for usage docs. Hosted-CLI and sub-agents have docs pre-loaded.)

canvasId.description: Canvas ID to get selection from. REQUIRED.

project.description: Optional: run THIS call against a project other than the session's bound one: a name or key from list_projects (or an unambiguous name/handle substring), or the absolute path of a project folder (one holding .bl files, or an empty one), which opens in the background and is added to list_projects. Unknown/ambiguous is refused with candidates.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export elements in the specified format and return the data. Raster formats (png, jpeg, webp) return an inline image. SVG returns raw SVG markup as text. HTML returns an HTML/CSS snippet as text. PDF returns base64-encoded data as text. Video formats (mp4, mov) write a file (large binary is never inlined) and return its path; use `duration` (seconds, max 30) and `fps` to control length. MOV supports a transparent background; MP4 does not. With `motion` (mp4/mov) it renders a FILM, `Motion/<film>.bm` beside the canvas or at the project root: STATE frames tweened by element name, per-frame blueprint patch lines for the procedural rest (knowledge `motion/core` and `motion/grammar`, runner `tool/motion/render.mjs`). "replay" (animated reveal) needs an interactive recording session and is not available headlessly: it returns a clear error. When outputPath is provided, writes to that file path instead and returns a confirmation. In the web editor there is no local filesystem: outputPath is not available (omit it and the data returns inline), and video export (mp4/mov) is not available at all (use png/jpeg/webp/svg/pdf/html, or export from the desktop app). (External MCP clients: call `init` first for usage docs. Hosted-CLI and sub-agents have docs pre-loaded.)

background.description: Background type: "clear" for transparent, "window" for window color. Defaults to "clear". Ignored for svg/pdf.

format.description: Export format: "png" (default), "jpeg", "webp", "svg", "pdf", "html" (snippet), "htmlDoc" (self-contained document), "htmlFlex" (snippet using semantic flexbox for auto-layout), "react" (JSX snippet pasteable into a .tsx file), or "mp4"/"mov" (video: writes a file, returns its path).

canvasId.description: Canvas ID to export from. REQUIRED, except with `pages` (each item names its canvas) and when every id or #ref lives on one canvas (that canvas is read).

ids.description: Element IDs (or #refs) to export. REQUIRED, except with `motion` (a film names its own canvases) or `pages`. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

anyOf.description: Element IDs (or #refs) to export. REQUIRED, except with `motion` (a film names its own canvases) or `pages`. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

pages.description: pdf: one page per item, in order: an element id or #ref (the element, a frame exactly its frame) or a canvas path (the whole canvas), on any canvas. Replaces `ids`; the format defaults to pdf.

anyOf.description: pdf: one page per item, in order: an element id or #ref (the element, a frame exactly its frame) or a canvas path (the whole canvas), on any canvas. Replaces `ids`; the format defaults to pdf.

duration.description: Video duration in seconds (default 3, max 30). Only used for mp4/mov.

anyOf.description: Video duration in seconds (default 3, max 30). Only used for mp4/mov.

fps.description: Video frames per second (default 30, clamped 1-60). Only used for mp4/mov.

anyOf.description: Video frames per second (default 30, clamped 1-60). Only used for mp4/mov.

scale.description: Scale factor for raster export. Defaults to 2.0. Ignored for svg/pdf. Mutually exclusive with width/height.

anyOf.description: Scale factor for raster export. Defaults to 2.0. Ignored for svg/pdf. Mutually exclusive with width/height.

width.description: Target pixel width for raster export. If only width is provided, height is computed to maintain aspect ratio. Mutually exclusive with scale. Ignored for svg/pdf.

anyOf.description: Target pixel width for raster export. If only width is provided, height is computed to maintain aspect ratio. Mutually exclusive with scale. Ignored for svg/pdf.

height.description: Target pixel height for raster export. If only height is provided, width is computed to maintain aspect ratio. Mutually exclusive with scale. Ignored for svg/pdf.

anyOf.description: Target pixel height for raster export. If only height is provided, width is computed to maintain aspect ratio. Mutually exclusive with scale. Ignored for svg/pdf.

fitMode.description: How to fit content when both width and height are specified: "fit" (letterbox, default), "fill" (crop), "stretch" (ignore aspect ratio).

jpegQuality.description: JPEG quality 0-100. Defaults to 90. Only used when format is "jpeg".

anyOf.description: JPEG quality 0-100. Defaults to 90. Only used when format is "jpeg".

webpQuality.description: WebP quality 0-100. Defaults to 90. Only used when format is "webp" and webpLossless is false.

anyOf.description: WebP quality 0-100. Defaults to 90. Only used when format is "webp" and webpLossless is false.

webpLossless.description: When true, uses WebP lossless encoding (quality is ignored). Defaults to false. Only used when format is "webp".

anyOf.description: When true, uses WebP lossless encoding (quality is ignored). Defaults to false. Only used when format is "webp".

videoQuality.description: mp4/mov: "low", "medium" or "high" (default high), the encoder bits per pixel per frame 0.04, 0.08 or 0.16 (VideoBitrate: 5, 10 or 20 Mbps at 1080p60, bounded 1 to 120 Mbps): a 29 s 1440x1440x60 clip asks about 20 Mbps at high, about 72 MB, half at medium, a quarter at low. The answer names the applied bitrate.

videoMaxBytes.description: mp4/mov: a size target in bytes (a 16 MB cap is 16000000). The encoder takes the bitrate that fits it over the clip when that is under the quality's ask, so one export lands under it, no second pass. Subtract the audio you will mux yourself. The answer names the applied bitrate and notes an overshoot.

anyOf.description: mp4/mov: a size target in bytes (a 16 MB cap is 16000000). The encoder takes the bitrate that fits it over the clip when that is under the quality's ask, so one export lands under it, no second pass. Subtract the audio you will mux yourself. The answer names the applied bitrate and notes an overshoot.

union.description: png/jpeg/webp: inline elements far apart on the canvas (their union mostly empty space) come back as one close-up per element; true keeps one image of the whole union.

anyOf.description: png/jpeg/webp: inline elements far apart on the canvas (their union mostly empty space) come back as one close-up per element; true keeps one image of the whole union.

outputPath.description: File path to write the exported data to. When provided, writes the file and returns a confirmation instead of inline data. A relative path is written under the project's Exports/ folder; a path ending in / names a folder. Works with all formats.

htmlImages.description: HTML/React only. Pictures are resampled to the size they are drawn at (1x and 2x, an image-set) and deduped. "files" (the default with outputPath) writes them under images/ beside the markup; "inline" embeds data URIs (always the case without outputPath).

htmlKeepInvisible.description: HTML/React only, for films: an element at opacity 0 is kept as markup at opacity 0 (it fades or cuts in later) instead of being dropped. Default false.

anyOf.description: HTML/React only, for films: an element at opacity 0 is kept as markup at opacity 0 (it fades or cuts in later) instead of being dropped. Default false.

motion.description: mp4/mov only: render a FILM through the engine evaluator (knowledge `motion/core`). Pass the film's name, "Launch" (or "Motion/Launch.bm"): `Motion/<film>.bm` in the folder of canvasId or at the project root, written by an edit whose ```bm fence opens with file("Motion/<film>.bm"). Or an object {film: "<name>" | bm: "<text>", patches: [[t, [lines]], ...], tracks: ["<track line>", ...] (a compiled track program the engine evaluates at any t), frames: [a, b], motionBlur: 1..8, frameHashes: true, dumpFrames: {dir, frames}}. A film's states live on the canvases its canvases[...] line names. `fps` defaults to the film's header.

sessionId.description: Session ID for per-session visual feedback. Optional.

project.description: Optional: run THIS call against a project other than the session's bound one: a name or key from list_projects (or an unambiguous name/handle substring), or the absolute path of a project folder (one holding .bl files, or an empty one), which opens in the background and is added to list_projects. Unknown/ambiguous is refused with candidates.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the project's documents, each answered as the fence you would send back through edit: a canvas as ```bl with file(path) first and its rows (ids bound), a film as ```bm, a design system as ```ds. A canvas answer lists the films that name it above its fence (`films: Motion/Launch.bm`). Pass `paths` (canvas paths such as "Projects/Dashboard", "Motion/Launch.bm", "Styles/default.ds"), `ids` (element ids or #refs, with their canvas in paths) and/or the filters (query, textContent, type, fillColor, componentName) to find elements across canvases. `format` is "blueprint" (default), "summary" (compact metadata) or "skeleton" (summary plus the tokenRefs, no geometry), the fence the carrier. (External MCP clients: call `init` first for usage docs. Hosted-CLI and sub-agents have docs pre-loaded.)

paths.description: The documents to read: canvas paths (e.g. "Projects/Dashboard", .bl optional), films ("Motion/Launch.bm") and design systems ("Styles/default.ds"). Omit with a filter to search every canvas.

anyOf.description: The documents to read: canvas paths (e.g. "Projects/Dashboard", .bl optional), films ("Motion/Launch.bm") and design systems ("Styles/default.ds"). Omit with a filter to search every canvas.

ids.description: Element IDs (or #refs) to read, the same as listing them in `scope`. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

anyOf.description: Element IDs (or #refs) to read, the same as listing them in `scope`. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

disk.description: true answers from the saved .bl files on a background isolate: it never loads, opens or writes a canvas, whatever its size, so a heavy or closed canvas is safe to read. Rows come as stored, one header per canvas names its row count and bytes, and a canvas open in the app says a change not saved yet is not here. Takes paths (omit to search every canvas), ids, the filters, depth, limit (rows, default 200) and the disk-only pattern, ancestors, subtree, consumersOf.

anyOf.description: true answers from the saved .bl files on a background isolate: it never loads, opens or writes a canvas, whatever its size, so a heavy or closed canvas is safe to read. Rows come as stored, one header per canvas names its row count and bytes, and a canvas open in the app says a change not saved yet is not here. Takes paths (omit to search every canvas), ids, the filters, depth, limit (rows, default 200) and the disk-only pattern, ancestors, subtree, consumersOf.

pattern.description: With disk: a regular expression over each stored row, for what the filters leave unnamed (a font size, a token, an override).

ancestors.description: With disk: each matched row carries its parent chain, board first.

anyOf.description: With disk: each matched row carries its parent chain, board first.

subtree.description: With disk: each matched row carries its descendants, bounded by depth.

anyOf.description: With disk: each matched row carries its descendants, bounded by depth.

consumersOf.description: With disk: the id of a component master. Answers each canvas holding a copy of it: the copies, and the canvas row count to weigh a master edit. Set a master's id, not a variant child, for the copies of that master.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring match on element name AND canvas path. Element matches answer as fences; canvas matches ride the `canvases:` line. Canvas matching only runs when no `paths` are given. With a design system in `paths`, its statements whose token name contains it.

textContent.description: Case-insensitive substring match on text element content.

type.description: Filter by element type. One of: vector, line, circle, rectangle, text, parent.

fillColor.description: Find elements with a fill matching this hex color (e.g. "#FFCC00" for yellow). Perceptual color matching, close shades are included.

componentName.description: Find instances of a component whose master name contains this substring (case-insensitive).

format.description: Output shape per canvas, inside its fence. "blueprint" (default) is the rows with their ids, what edit takes back. "summary" is compact metadata (id, name, type, parentId, parentName, childCount, text snippet). "skeleton" adds the design-system tokenRefs and omits geometry.

depth.description: Subtree depth per match, in every format. 0 = matched element only, 1 = + immediate children, etc. Omitted: unlimited for "blueprint", the matched elements only for "summary" and "skeleton" (each record names its parentId).

anyOf.description: Subtree depth per match, in every format. 0 = matched element only, 1 = + immediate children, etc. Omitted: unlimited for "blueprint", the matched elements only for "summary" and "skeleton" (each record names its parentId).

expandInstances.description: READ-ONLY. When true (with format="blueprint"), a component instance is not collapsed to its compact inst() line: its derived children are shown as full lines with their REAL ids so you can inspect and target them (via read/execute_commands). Those children are managed by the master and are read-only; a change to them is a change to override(...) on the instance. Default false (the compact inst() form). Bounded by `depth` like any subtree.

anyOf.description: READ-ONLY. When true (with format="blueprint"), a component instance is not collapsed to its compact inst() line: its derived children are shown as full lines with their REAL ids so you can inspect and target them (via read/execute_commands). Those children are managed by the master and are read-only; a change to them is a change to override(...) on the instance. Default false (the compact inst() form). Bounded by `depth` like any subtree.

full.description: READ-ONLY. When true (with format="blueprint"), return the COMPLETE vector geometry even for a large path. Default false: a vector whose blueprint would blow the per-readback token budget is summarized to node count + bounds + this flag as its continuation door (a one-line note names what was elided). Set true to inspect the full node/edge graph of one big vector; scope it to that element to keep the readback bounded.

anyOf.description: READ-ONLY. When true (with format="blueprint"), return the COMPLETE vector geometry even for a large path. Default false: a vector whose blueprint would blow the per-readback token budget is summarized to node count + bounds + this flag as its continuation door (a one-line note names what was elided). Set true to inspect the full node/edge graph of one big vector; scope it to that element to keep the readback bounded.

limit.description: Max top-level matches across all canvases. Defaults to 50. It applies with explicit element IDs too.

anyOf.description: Max top-level matches across all canvases. Defaults to 50. It applies with explicit element IDs too.

sessionId.description: Your session id from init: #refs resolve per session.

project.description: Optional: run THIS call against a project other than the session's bound one: a name or key from list_projects (or an unambiguous name/handle substring), or the absolute path of a project folder (one holding .bl files, or an empty one), which opens in the background and is added to list_projects. Unknown/ambiguous is refused with candidates.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List every project this user owns, each with its display name, key (a folder path or brilliant-cloud:// key), backing (local/synced/cloud), open state (active tab / background tab / closed), canvas count when known, and whether it is published, with its url, visibility, audience and your role where known. Pass a name or key from this list as the `project` argument on `init` or any canvas tool to work in a project other than the one on screen, including a closed one.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit the project's documents. `text` holds one or more fences, applied in order: ```bl (a canvas, blueprint rows: omit ids for new elements, lead with an id or #ref to modify, delete(#ref) to remove, preview(#a, #b) as a row for a screenshot), ```html (a canvas, HTML with inline CSS converted to elements), ```ds (a design system, statements spliced), ```bm (a film, the whole document replaced). The first row of every fence is file(path): file("Projects/Launch"), file("Styles/default.ds"), file("Motion/Launch.bm"). A call holds fences on any number of documents, canvases included, applied in order, one result entry per fence; a #ref and a `// label` checkpoint belong to the canvas of their fence. A bl fence's rows apply as they go and the first bad row halts with one line. The answer is the block result: the canvas fact, what changed, the refs, the diagnostics, the notes and a screenshot of the preview row. Pass your sessionId from init. (External MCP clients: call `init` first for usage docs. Hosted-CLI and sub-agents have docs pre-loaded.)

text.description: The fences: ```<bl|bm|ds|html> on its own line, file(path) as the first row, the rows, ``` on its own line. Several fences in one text apply in order.

background.description: Optional. true answers a `job:` id at once and runs the call on; wait({job}) blocks until it ends and answers its result. An edit waits its turn behind other agents' writes instead of refusing. Use it for a call that may outlast your client's timeout.

anyOf.description: Optional. true answers a `job:` id at once and runs the call on; wait({job}) blocks until it ends and answers its result. An edit waits its turn behind other agents' writes instead of refusing. Use it for a call that may outlast your client's timeout.

textFile.description: Instead of text: the absolute path of a local file holding the fences, for a block a script generated. Same pipeline and same answer as text, plus a `job:` line. With no requestId the id is a hash of the bytes, so resending the same file after a timeout converges on the first answer; a file whose bytes changed is a new request. Desktop only.

sessionId.description: Your session id from init (refs and design-system state are per session).

requestId.description: Optional idempotency key. Pass a stable, unique id for this logical request and REUSE the SAME id if you retry after a timeout or relay error: the retry converges on the original result instead of applying a second time. The id is one request: for 2 minutes after a success, a call reusing it with the same text answers the first result, and with different text is refused with nothing applied, so new text takes a new id.

response_mode.description: Optional. "full" (default) answers the block result with the blueprint of every affected element, or a read handle when that blueprint runs past 50 rows. "compact" answers the block result with a read handle instead of the blueprint, names up to 6 changed elements (past 6, 5 and a count), and keeps every warning, error and new ref.

project.description: Optional: run THIS call against a project other than the session's bound one: a name or key from list_projects (or an unambiguous name/handle substring), or the absolute path of a project folder (one holding .bl files, or an empty one), which opens in the background and is added to list_projects. Unknown/ambiguous is refused with candidates.

designSystem.description: Optional. Design-system mode for this and all later calls (sticky, once set it persists until changed). One of: `"default"` (use the project default DS, token discipline enforced, no bare hex/numerics on tokenizable slots); `"new"` (author your own DS, write a ```ds fence before any bl rows); `"none"` (sovereign, bare hex/numeric values allowed); or the name of a brand YOU authored earlier this session. Omit to keep the current mode (external sessions default to `"none"`).

tools.name: create_modify_elements
tools.description: Retired. A call answers the one line that names the door: edit({ text }) to write, read({ paths }) to read.

tools.name: create_html
tools.description: Retired. A call answers the one line that names the door: edit({ text }) to write, read({ paths }) to read.

tools.name: lookup
tools.description: Retired. A call answers the one line that names the door: edit({ text }) to write, read({ paths }) to read.

tools.name: read_objects_result
tools.description: Retired. A call answers the one line that names the door: edit({ text }) to write, read({ paths }) to read.

tools.name: objects_result
tools.description: Retired. A call answers the one line that names the door: edit({ text }) to write, read({ paths }) to read.

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Wait for a long call to end, instead of sleeping and checking. `job` is the id from a `background: true` call of edit, export or render_ui, or the requestId (or `job:` line) of an edit, also one whose call timed out on your side. Blocks until the job is done or failed and answers its result, the answer the call itself would have given. `running` means your timeout ran out and the job goes on: call wait again. `superseded` means the job ended with an earlier app run or its answer aged out: read the canvas. If this call cannot reach the app at all, the app is down: run scripts/mcp-wait-up.sh.

timeout.description: Seconds to block, default 120, at most 280. 0 answers the state now.

anyOf.description: Seconds to block, default 120, at most 280. 0 answers the state now.

sessionId.description: Your session id from init: a requestId is per session.

tools.name: convert_html
tools.description: Convert HTML with inline CSS to Brilliant blueprint lines WITHOUT creating anything: the exact lines edit (html) would write, per input string, plus the converter's notes. Batch many strings (the frames of a composition) in one call as `frames`. With `layout: true` each frame is also built into a throwaway world and the answer adds every element's laid-out box (x, y, w, h in canvas px, the unrotated box), its rotation, opacity, first solid fill, name, type and text, so the layout is the app's auto layout, never a guess. A `data-id` or `data-key` attribute is the element's NAME (stable identity across frames, the handle a motion patch line leads with as #name); `id="x"` is a #x ref as in edit (html). Give the outermost element an explicit px width and height so percentage sizes and offsets resolve. Same CSS support as edit (html), plus transform translate()/scale()/rotate() (fractional degrees) folded into p()/s()/rot().

frames.description: HTML strings to convert, one per frame, in order. At most 1000 per call and 16 MiB in total.

anyOf.description: HTML strings to convert, one per frame, in order. At most 1000 per call and 16 MiB in total.

html.description: One HTML string (the one-frame form of `frames`).

layout.description: true: build each frame into a throwaway world and answer the laid-out boxes (`elements` per frame). Default false.

anyOf.description: true: build each frame into a throwaway world and answer the laid-out boxes (`elements` per frame). Default false.

tokens.description: true: add the project's design-system tokens resolved per mode as `tokens` (`{ modes, values: { base, light, dark: { key: hex or number } } }`), with or without frames. Default false.

anyOf.description: true: add the project's design-system tokens resolved per mode as `tokens` (`{ modes, values: { base, light, dark: { key: hex or number } } }`), with or without frames. Default false.

project.description: Optional: with `layout` or `tokens`, resolve against a project other than the session's bound one (its fonts and design system), a name or key from list_projects.

tools.name: execute_commands
tools.description: Execute one or more commands by ID. Accepts an array of commands that share a single canvasId. Commands run sequentially, stopping on first error. Use command IDs from the skill docs. Pass previewIds + previewScale: 2 for inline PNG verification. Visually inspect every preview, describe what you see, fix issues. (External MCP clients: call `init` first for usage docs. Hosted-CLI and sub-agents have docs pre-loaded.)

canvasId.description: Target canvas ID. Required for every canvas-scoped verb (enforced at dispatch, refused by name when missing); the workspace/app-level verbs (get_canvases, create_canvas, create_folder, list_keybindings, the library acts, ...) are exempt and need none.

commands.description: Array of commands to execute sequentially.

anyOf.description: Array of commands to execute sequentially.

ids.description: Element IDs (or #refs) to operate on. A command that needs targets and resolves none is refused, never silently no-oped. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

anyOf.description: Element IDs (or #refs) to operate on. A command that needs targets and resolves none is refused, never silently no-oped. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.
Command-specific parameters (color, value, etc.).

parts.description: Part targets in place of ids: element id (or #ref) to its parts [{type, id}], type "fill", "stroke" or "region". A fill or stroke id is the first item of its tuple in `read` output, f[(<id>,...)]; a region id is its vr(rN) short id. One fill: {"#a": [{"type": "fill", "id": "<fill id>"}]}.

anyOf.description: Part targets in place of ids: element id (or #ref) to its parts [{type, id}], type "fill", "stroke" or "region". A fill or stroke id is the first item of its tuple in `read` output, f[(<id>,...)]; a region id is its vr(rN) short id. One fill: {"#a": [{"type": "fill", "id": "<fill id>"}]}.

ids.description: Optional: element IDs applied to every command in the batch that names none of its own. The per-command `commands[i].ids` always wins. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

anyOf.description: Optional: element IDs applied to every command in the batch that names none of its own. The per-command `commands[i].ids` always wins. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

previewIds.description: Element IDs to include in a PNG preview returned alongside the summary. Omit for no preview.

anyOf.description: Element IDs to include in a PNG preview returned alongside the summary. Omit for no preview.

previewScale.description: Scale factor for the preview image (default 1.0, max 3.0). Use 2.0 for verifying visual details like text or alignment.

anyOf.description: Scale factor for the preview image (default 1.0, max 3.0). Use 2.0 for verifying visual details like text or alignment.

sessionId.description: Session ID for per-session visual feedback. Optional.

project.description: Optional: run THIS call against a project other than the session's bound one: a name or key from list_projects (or an unambiguous name/handle substring), or the absolute path of a project folder (one holding .bl files, or an empty one), which opens in the background and is added to list_projects. Unknown/ambiguous is refused with candidates.

tools.name: get_knowledge
tools.description: Load design knowledge by key. Blueprint DSL work loads it first; an html fence needs none. Pass keys from the available keys list returned by init (e.g. "blueprint/core", "design/colors", "effects/glass"). By default a key also pulls in its prerequisite docs (its `assumes:` deps); the response names them under "Also auto-loaded" so you can see what was bundled. Pass `includeDependencies: false` to load ONLY the keys you name (the skipped prerequisites are listed so you can request them deliberately).

keys.description: List of knowledge keys to load. See available keys returned by init.

anyOf.description: List of knowledge keys to load. See available keys returned by init.

items.description: Knowledge key (e.g. "blueprint/core", "design/colors", "effects/glass"). See available keys returned by init.

includeDependencies.description: Whether to auto-load each key's prerequisite docs (its `assumes:` deps). Default true. Set false to load exactly the keys you name and nothing else; the response lists the prerequisites it skipped so you can request them explicitly.

anyOf.description: Whether to auto-load each key's prerequisite docs (its `assumes:` deps). Default true. Set false to load exactly the keys you name and nothing else; the response lists the prerequisites it skipped so you can request them explicitly.

sessionId.description: Session ID for per-session tracking. Optional.

tools.name: init
tools.description: Bootstrap a design session. Returns a unique session ID, session context (canvas ID, repo path), and documentation. Call this first. Pass the returned session ID as the `sessionId` argument on every subsequent `edit` / `read` call: this scopes your refs/design-system state AND gives you your own distinct labelled cursor on the canvas (concurrent agents that echo their IDs never share one cursor). Optionally pass a short `agentName` (2-3 words) to label that cursor. Pass `project` (a name or key from `list_projects`) to bind this session to a project OTHER than the one on screen — including a project that is not open, which the agent reaches headlessly, or the absolute path of a project folder Brilliant has not seen yet (a new Git worktree), which it opens and lists. If you CANNOT read images, pass `vision: false`: preview requests then return a textual render summary instead of an inline PNG. Then write with `edit`: an ```html fence for most tasks (no knowledge loading needed), a ```bl fence (Blueprint DSL) for advanced features and edits, with its knowledge loaded first via `get_knowledge`.

agentName.description: Optional short display name (2-3 words) for this agent's canvas cursor. Clipped to 32 characters.

vision.description: Whether this client can READ inline images (default true). Set false if you cannot see images: preview requests (a `preview()` row) then return a compact TEXTUAL render summary: each element's bounds in parent and world space, layout/overflow checks, and a fill/text one-liner, in place of the inline PNG, so you can verify your write landed without seeing it.

anyOf.description: Whether this client can READ inline images (default true). Set false if you cannot see images: preview requests (a `preview()` row) then return a compact TEXTUAL render summary: each element's bounds in parent and world space, layout/overflow checks, and a fill/text one-liner, in place of the inline PNG, so you can verify your write landed without seeing it.

project.description: Optional project to bind this session to: an exact name or key from `list_projects`, or an unambiguous name/handle substring, or the absolute path of a project folder (one holding .bl files, or an empty one), which opens in the background and is added to list_projects. Defaults to the project currently on screen. An ambiguous or unknown value is refused with the candidates listed.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate an AI image and apply it as a fill on targetElementId. Target element must already exist — create it first (top-level hosted-CLI agents: emit an `<edit>` block; sub-agents and external MCP clients: call `edit`), then call generate_image with that element's id or #ref. Call get_knowledge(["images/prompts","images/integration","images/references"]) for prompt engineering, quality presets, and parallel-generation guidance. Runs on your own Google key when one is set (Settings > Your own AI > Google), otherwise on Brilliant AI for a signed-in account.

referenceElementIds.description: Element IDs to use as reference images (up to 14).

anyOf.description: Element IDs to use as reference images (up to 14).

aspectRatio.description: Output aspect ratio: "1:1" (default) | "16:9" | "9:16" | "4:3" | "3:4". In batch mode applies to every target unless a target overrides it.

targetElementId.description: Element ID to apply the image fill to. Required unless targets is provided.

targets.description: Batch mode: generate multiple images in parallel (preferred when generating 2+).

anyOf.description: Batch mode: generate multiple images in parallel (preferred when generating 2+).

sessionId.description: Session ID for per-session visual feedback. Optional.

tools.name: generate_svg
tools.description: Generate editable vector graphics (SVG) from a text prompt and place them on the canvas as native editable shapes. Use for icons, logos, illustrations, diagrams — anything that should stay crisp and remain editable. For photos / realistic images use `generate_image` instead. Optional `referenceElementIds` (up to 4) export to PNG and steer style. Use `n` (1–4) for parallel variations of a single prompt, or `targets` to fan out distinct prompts in parallel. Call get_knowledge(["svg/prompts","svg/integration"]) for prompt patterns and decision rules. Requires Quiver API key.

prompt.description: Natural-language description of the SVG to generate.

instructions.description: Optional style/behavior instructions for the model.

intent.description: A short present-tense line shown beside your cursor while the vector is drawn, e.g. 'Sketching a fox logo'. Optional; derived from the prompt when absent.

referenceElementIds.description: Element IDs to export as PNG and pass as style references (up to 4).

anyOf.description: Element IDs to export as PNG and pass as style references (up to 4).

n.description: Number of variations from the single prompt (1–4, default 1). Cheaper than `targets` because it is one API call.

anyOf.description: Number of variations from the single prompt (1–4, default 1). Cheaper than `targets` because it is one API call.

targets.description: Batch mode: distinct prompts generated in parallel. Use for multiple different SVGs (e.g. "search icon", "settings icon").

anyOf.description: Batch mode: distinct prompts generated in parallel. Use for multiple different SVGs (e.g. "search icon", "settings icon").

sessionId.description: Session ID for per-session visual feedback. Optional.

tools.name: vectorize_image
tools.description: Convert a raster image element on the canvas into editable vector paths. The new vector elements are placed on the canvas; the original raster element is left untouched (delete it manually if no longer needed). Use for: importing PNG/JPEG content the user wants to edit as vectors, cleaning up screenshots into icons, or converting AI-generated raster images into editable shapes. Requires Quiver API key.

sourceElementId.description: Element ID (or `#ref`) of the raster element to vectorize. Required.

autoCrop.description: Auto-crop the source image before vectorizing (default true).

anyOf.description: Auto-crop the source image before vectorizing (default true).

sessionId.description: Session ID for per-session visual feedback. Optional.

tools.name: remove_background
tools.description: Remove the background from real photos on the canvas: the subject keeps its exact pixels (the real face, the real product) and the background becomes transparent, in place, in the same image fill (crop, scale mode and opacity kept). Use it instead of generate_image whenever the image is a real photo and the user wants it cut out: "a real photo, keep the pixels, cut the background". generate_image regenerates the picture and invents new pixels. `ids`: the element ids (or #refs) whose image fills to cut (a frame, group or instance id reaches every image inside it); one request per distinct image. A cut fill reads back as img(<cutout>, ..., src(<original>)); execute_commands restore_background puts the original back. Answers the new asset path per element, or the named failure (no subject, allowance used, lane unavailable, image missing). add_cutout_outline then traces an outline around the cut subject. Runs on Brilliant AI: a signed-in account's Brilliant AI usage; in the built-in chat, a signed-out user gets the free daily cutouts of the /remove-background page with no account, and is told when they are used up.

ids.description: Element IDs (or #refs) holding the image fills to cut; a frame, group or instance id cuts every image inside it. Required.

anyOf.description: Element IDs (or #refs) holding the image fills to cut; a frame, group or instance id cuts every image inside it. Required.

tools.name: add_cutout_outline
tools.description: Add an outline around the subject of an image whose background was removed (remove_background first): the cutout's visible edge is traced into a new vector element placed directly above the image, aligned with its crop, rotation, flip and scale; stroke only, no fill, outside stroke, round joins (the sticker look). The outline is an ordinary element afterwards (restyle, move or delete it). `ids`: the image element ids (or #refs; a frame, group or instance id reaches the cut images inside it). `color`: optional #RRGGBB stroke color (default plain white). `width`: optional stroke width in px (default 2 percent of the image's short edge). Answers the new outline id per image, or the honest refusal (no removed background, nothing visible to trace, a tiled image). Runs locally: no Brilliant AI usage.

ids.description: Element IDs (or #refs) of images whose background was removed. Required.

anyOf.description: Element IDs (or #refs) of images whose background was removed. Required.
Stroke width in px. Optional.

tools.name: capture_ui
tools.description: Screenshot a part of Brilliant's own UI (a toolbar, the palette / color picker, a panel) to an image file. Optionally stage commands to drive the UI into a state first, and draw highlight boxes over sub-targets. `target` is a capture-registry id such as "full-ui", "top-toolbar", "left-toolbar", "right-toolbar", "bottom-toolbar", "command-palette", or "ai-chat-panel". Chrome only by default on every host (the canvas area is left empty); pass includeCanvas:true (full-ui only) to composite the GPU canvas underneath. Writes lossless WebP by default. Desktop-only: it writes an image file, so it is not available in the web editor.

target.description: Capture-registry id to screenshot (e.g. "command-palette"). REQUIRED. "full-ui" is the whole window: menus, dropdowns, popovers, tooltips and dialogs included (they mount above the panels), so photograph an open menu with target "full-ui" and cropTo its panel; a panel target never contains its own open menu.

stageCommands.description: Ordered commands to drive the UI into the desired state before capturing. Same command IDs execute_commands accepts. Executed sequentially; a failure aborts the capture.

anyOf.description: Ordered commands to drive the UI into the desired state before capturing. Same command IDs execute_commands accepts. Executed sequentially; a failure aborts the capture.
Optional command params (value, color, etc.).

canvasId.description: Canvas the command targets (most commands require one). May also be supplied inside "args".

ids.description: Elements the command targets, if any. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

anyOf.description: Elements the command targets, if any. `elementIds` is accepted as an alias.

settleMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after staging before capturing (default 300).

anyOf.description: Milliseconds to wait after staging before capturing (default 300).
Device-pixel scale for the capture (default 2).

includeCanvas.description: Composite the GPU canvas front buffer under the chrome. Only meaningful for target "full-ui". Default false.

anyOf.description: Composite the GPU canvas front buffer under the chrome. Only meaningful for target "full-ui". Default false.

highlights.description: Boxes to draw over the capture. Each is either {target: "<registry-id>"} or {rect: [x, y, w, h]} in captured-image logical pixels.

anyOf.description: Boxes to draw over the capture. Each is either {target: "<registry-id>"} or {rect: [x, y, w, h]} in captured-image logical pixels.

rect.description: [x, y, w, h] in captured-image logical pixels.

anyOf.description: [x, y, w, h] in captured-image logical pixels.

dimBackground.description: Dim everything outside the highlight rects to 35% black. Default false.

anyOf.description: Dim everything outside the highlight rects to 35% black. Default false.

cropTo.description: Capture-registry id to crop the result down to. When set, "target" MUST be "full-ui": the full UI is captured (so the panel renders over the real backdrop with true colors), then cropped to this id's on-screen rect. Use this instead of capturing a panel boundary directly, which renders translucent chrome without its backdrop.

cropMargin.description: Logical pixels to expand the cropTo rect on all sides (clamped to image bounds). Default 0.

anyOf.description: Logical pixels to expand the cropTo rect on all sides (clamped to image bounds). Default 0.

outputPath.description: Absolute file path to write the image to. REQUIRED.

tools.name: list_capture_targets
tools.description: List the capture-registry ids currently mounted in Brilliant's UI (the valid "target"/"cropTo"/highlight ids for capture_ui). Takes no arguments. Returns a sorted JSON array; each entry is {id, mounted, rect: [x, y, w, h] in logical global pixels, children: [nested ids]}.

tools.name: render_ui
tools.description: Render a Brilliant UI component into an EXACT declarative state and capture it to an image file, offscreen, without touching the live app. `component` is a stager id (call list_stagers to enumerate them and their state schemas); `state` is the component-specific declarative state. Optionally draw highlight boxes over sub-targets (the scene registers "ui-stage.*" ids) and override the stage size. Writes lossless WebP by default. Desktop-only: it writes an image file, so it is not available in the web editor.

tools.description: List the UI Stage components render_ui can render, with each component's default logical size and its declarative state schema. Takes no arguments. Returns a JSON array; each entry is {component, defaultSize: [w, h], stateSchema}.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Open the Brilliant feedback card for the user to review and send. This does NOT send: the card opens, the user presses Send, and you tell them it is open and waiting (never claim it was sent). `message` is OPTIONAL (pre-fill a draft or open empty); `attachments` is tolerated but ignored (nothing about the user's world is ever attached). Feedback is a routing decision, not one surface, and consent scales with what leaves the machine: the user's words move by the user's act, the user's context moves only per-item opt-in, and your own observations ride telemetry, never GitHub or email. Offer it proactively, once and calmly (at most once per session AND once per class), when you hit a wall or a missing capability, when the user asks for something the product cannot do, or when the user is frustrated. Before running the routing flow (card vs GitHub issue vs email vs Discord), load the full playbook with get_knowledge(["reference/feedback"]).

message.description: OPTIONAL. The drafted feedback message, in the user's own framing (the user can edit it before sending). Omit to open an empty card.

attachments.description: Ignored in this version; accepted for backward compatibility (nothing about the user's world is ever attached).

anyOf.description: Ignored in this version; accepted for backward compatibility (nothing about the user's world is ever attached).
